heading: 5. Pattern: Implementing a Custom Data Type
text: - **Coercer**: the runtime converts values through one `ExtendableCoercer` per model (`hu.blackbelt.mapper.api`): `coerce(sourceValue, Class<T>)` or `coerce(sourceValue, String className)`. A `Converter` has `getSourceType()`, `getTargetType()` and `apply(Object)`. `DataTypeManager.registerCustomType(...)` adds the converters you pass to that coercer, so `coerce("...", YourType.class)` works afterwards. In OSGi, `ExtendableCoercerService` also picks up every `Converter` registered as an OSGi service.

heading: 5. Pattern: Implementing a Custom Data Type
text:
- **Service and properties**: `DataTypeManager` is one OSGi service per model. It is registered with the property `judo.model.name=<model name>`, which is why the `@Reference` target is `(judo.model.name=<app>)` (the same property the `AsmModel` service carries). Register each custom type once: a second `registerCustomType` for the same `EDataType` throws `IllegalStateException("Custom type already registered")`, so call `unregisterCustomType(modelType)` in `@Deactivate`.
- **Formatter overload**: `registerCustomType(modelType, javaClassName, converters, formatter)` takes a `Formatter<T>` (`getType()`, `convertValueToString`, `parseString`) and adds both `T -> String` and `String -> T` converters from it, so no hand-written `Converter` is needed.

heading: Time and Time Zones
text: - Generated UI columns and fields format timestamps in the **browser** time zone (the React template calls `Intl.DateTimeFormat` without a `timeZone`). A string built in a model expression uses `defaultZoneId`, so the same instant shows with the zone offset between the two (for example `18:00` in a model-built string and `20:00` in a history column). The model cannot read the browser zone: show the timestamp itself in the UI and avoid a derived string that formats it.

heading: Binary Upload Tokens
text:
### FileStore Java API

Custom Java code reads and writes binary content through the OSGi service `hu.blackbelt.osgi.filestore.api.FileStoreService`:

- `String put(InputStream data, String fileName, String mimeType)` stores the content and returns the file id.
- `InputStream get(String fileId)`, `boolean exists(String fileId)`.
- `getMimeType(fileId)`, `getFileName(fileId)`, `long getSize(fileId)`, `Date getCreateTime(fileId)`, `URL getAccessUrl(fileId)`, `getProtocol()`.

A binary attribute value in generated Java is `hu.blackbelt.judo.dispatcher.api.FileType` (Lombok `@Builder`, getters): `id`, `fileName`, `size` (`Long`), `mimeType`. It is persisted as a JSON string `{"id":..,"fileName":..,"size":..,"mimeType":..}`. To attach a file from Java, `put` the content and set a `FileType` built with the returned id, name, size and MIME type.

The backend is chosen with `JUDO_PLATFORM_FILESTORE`: `filesystem` (directory `filestoreDirectory`, default `$HOME/file-store`), `rdbms` (table `FILESTORE`) or `s3`. Any other value, including a typo, disables the file store and the upload/download endpoints. `JUDO_PLATFORM_FILESTORE_TOKEN_EXPIRY` sets the upload token lifetime in minutes (`0` = no expiry).

heading: See Also
text:
## Initializer Operations

An operation with `initializer = true` (an ESM `Operation` flag, not `OperationType.INITIALIZER`) is run by the platform; nobody calls it.

- **Shape**: `STATIC`, no input (validation `InitializerOperationIsValid`).
- **When**: in the OSGi runtime, `InitScriptExecutor` runs every initializer synchronously when the model's component activates, after the SDK operations and the identity manager are ready. It runs on **every** start of the model bundle, not once per deploy, so write initializers idempotently (check before create).
- **Identity**: `dispatcher.callOperation(name, exchange)` is called with an empty exchange: no principal and no `ACTOR`. Do not read the actor or rely on role-based access inside an initializer.
- **Transaction**: a script or custom (Java) operation is wrapped in `TransactionalOperationCall`, so each initializer runs in its own transaction.
- **Failure**: an exception is logged (`Initializer script <fqn> failed`) and the next initializer still runs; the `InitScriptsCompleted` service is registered only if all initializers succeeded.
- Spring Boot runtime: no caller of the initializer flag was found in the judo-ng sources (*verify* before relying on it there).

The generated `<Entity>Initializer.initBuilder()` Java interface belongs to the separate transfer-object initializer (`OperationType.INITIALIZER`), not to this flag.

heading: See Also
text:
## Scheduled Work

The platform has no scheduler: `judo-services-job` only runs the initializer operations at startup, and no Quartz or scheduling component exists in the judo-ng runtime sources. Periodic work is application code (for example an OSGi component with its own executor).

- A scheduler thread has no request context: no principal and no `ACTOR`.
- To get the platform's transaction and operation handling, call a modeled operation through the `Dispatcher` (`callOperation`) instead of using the DAO directly; script and custom operations run in their own transaction (see Initializer Operations).
- Do not rely on `ACTOR`-based access or variables in such a call: the exchange carries no actor unless you put one in.

Not settled by source: the behaviour of an application's own scheduler (Quartz or other) is outside the platform; no code read for a DAO call made outside the dispatcher.

heading: See Also
text:
## Email Service

Inject `hu.blackbelt.email.api.EmailService` (OSGi) and call `sendMessage(EmailMessage.emailBuilder()....build())` (or pass the builder):

- Fields: `from`, `tos`, `ccs`, `bccs` (sets), `replyTo`, `subject`, `plaintTemplate`, `htmlTemplate`, `model`.
- Attachments: `fileAttachments` / `inputStreamAttachments` (name -> `File` / `BinaryAttachment`); inline content: `fileInlinedContents` / `inputStreamInlinedContents` (content id -> ...). `BinaryAttachment` (`binaryAttachmentBuilder()`) holds `inputStream` or `bytes`, and `mimeType`.
- **Templates**: `plaintTemplate` and `htmlTemplate` are Handlebars strings compiled inline and applied to `model` (a `Map`, bean or object with fields). The `subject` is **not** a template. At least one of the two templates must be non-blank, otherwise the call throws `No HTML or Plain message defined`. With both, a multipart message is sent.
- Every address is validated; an invalid one throws `IllegalArgumentException("Email is not valid: ...")`.
- The call is synchronous and uses the SMTP settings of the platform (`JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_*`, mapped to `mail.smtp.*` JavaMail properties on the `JavaMailSenderActivator` configuration). With `JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER=true` a local log SMTP server receives the messages and only logs them.

heading: Pagination
text:
Generated query customizers (`dao.query()...`, per-relation `query<Rel>(...)`) page like this:

- `selectList()`, `selectList(Integer limit)`, `selectList(Integer limit, Integer offset)` (**limit first**).
- Keyset paging: `selectList(Integer limit, <Entity> lastItem)` and `selectList(Integer limit, <Entity> lastItem, Boolean reverse)`.
- `selectOne()` and `selectOne(Integer offset)`, both returning an `Optional`.

The DAO also has `getAll()`, `countAll()`, `existsById(id)`, `getById(id[, mask])` (an `Optional`) and `findAllById(Iterable<id>[, mask])` (a `List`; use it for a bulk fetch instead of looping `getById`). `TimeFilter` (`hu.blackbelt.judo.sdk.query`) filters a time-of-day attribute with `lessThan`, `lessOrEqualThan`, `greaterThan`, `greaterOrEqualThan`, `equalTo`, `notEqualTo` on a `LocalTime`; it is not an interval-overlap filter, so express overlap as two filters on a start and an end attribute.

Per multi-valued relation the DAO generates `count<Rel>(owner)`, `create<Rel>(owner, relatedObject|relatedObjects[, mask])` (returns the created target; only when create is allowed), `add<Rel>(owner, related|relatedList)` and `remove<Rel>(owner, related|relatedList)` (only when add / remove is allowed), and `getRangeOf<Rel>` / `countRangeOf<Rel>` for relations with a range. Single-valued relations generate `query<Rel>(id | identifier | owner[, mask])`. Which of these exist depends on the relation's kind and access flags.

Also correct best-practices/backend/dao-fluent-query-filter.md line 54: `selectList(offset, limit)` is `selectList(limit, offset)`, and `TimeFilter` is a time-of-day filter.

heading: Pattern 4: Partial Updates
replace: When updating an entity, use a mask to ensure you only modify the fields that have changed.
text: `update(entity)` and `update(entity, mask)` write only the attributes and relations that are **present in the entity's payload**. A field that was not loaded and not set is absent, so it is left unchanged in the database; the platform does not null it. The `mask` only selects what the returned entity contains (it is used for the read-back after the write), it does not limit what is written. `update` requires the identifier; defaults are applied only to payloads without one, so an update does not reset fields to model defaults.

heading: DataMember (row with `identifier`, line 66)
replace: If `true`, this attribute is part of the natural key for the entity.
text: If `true`, the runtime enforces that the attribute's value is unique among the stored instances (and `null` is not checked). Each `identifier` attribute is checked on its own: two identifier attributes are two separate unique constraints, not one composite key. A violation fails the create or update with `IDENTIFIER_ATTRIBUTE_UNIQUENESS_VIOLATION`. The check is made by the runtime (payload validator and a SQL check per declaring table on the inheritance chain), not by a database constraint, and covers duplicates inside one batch. Model a composite key as an extra stored attribute with a value you compute, or as a hand-written validation.

heading: Statements and syntax
text: - A script has no statement to raise a modeled fault and no way to call an OSGi service: the statements are declaration, call, `return`, `unset`, `delete`, `create`, block, `if`, `for` and `while`. Implement the operation in Java (a custom implementation) when it must throw a modeled fault or use a service. Whether a fault raised by an operation that the script calls reaches the caller unchanged is not verified.

heading: Anonymous vs Authenticated Behaviour
text: - **Exposing an operation without login**: put the operation's transfer object (or an access to it) on an `ActorType` that is effectively anonymous (`anonymous = true`, no principal, or an unmapped principal). Such an actor gets no `realm`, so `asm2keycloak` creates no realm or client for it, and the REST layer does not verify a bearer token for its paths: the call runs with no principal and no `ACTOR`. Everything reachable through that actor's accesses is public; keep them minimal and put guards in an interceptor or in the operation itself.

Not read: access control applied to a call with no principal outside the Keycloak interceptor.

heading: Anonymous vs Authenticated Behaviour
text: - **`isActiveExpression`**: a JQL expression on the principal entity (for example `self.active`, a boolean attribute). It is copied to the filter of the mapped actor transfer object type. The runtime resolves the actor from the token in two steps: the token's client (`azp`) selects the actor type, then the actor entity is looked up by claim (USERNAME, then EMAIL, then an identifier attribute) with a search on that actor type. An entity for which the expression is false is not found, and the call fails with `AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND`; the same error appears when no entity matches the claim. Only actors with a mapped principal are looked up (`ActorType` without principal has no filter).

heading: Relation member types (TRANSIENT row, line 170)
text: - **Transient relation on an unmapped transfer object**: the target of an unmapped transfer object's relation must be `AGGREGATION`. `relationKind=ASSOCIATION` fails validation with `Relation: <rel> (in: <TO>) must be aggregation if transient.` and `Unmapped transfer object type: <TO> can only have aggregation kind relations.` The CLI creates a relation with `relationKind=AGGREGATION` by default; `aggregation=true` is rejected as read-only, and `relationKind` is the field to set. When the target is also unmapped, the UI generator treats the relation as an inline transient relation (create is supported inline); a mapped target is chosen from existing instances.

Open: what `mutable input.<rel>` means for a transient relation in JCL, and exact widget (nested form vs picker), are not settled by source.

heading: CLI notes (line 122-123, Access / `fill`)
text: - **Access with list cardinality needs a table column.** `create -t Access --ns <Actor> --set target=<TO>` also creates `<TO>::<TO>_Table`. Until that table has a column, validation reports `Columns are not defined for the viewable table of <TO>` and the ESM model is invalid (`error esm Invalid model`, transform skipped). Add one: `create -t DataColumn --ns <TO>::<TO>_Table --set dataFeature=<TO>.<attribute>`, or run `fill <TO>`. `validate --strict` is deprecated: validation errors always exit non-zero.
